Subject: Spike in 502s + p99 latency on private cluster (production)

Hi Olga / Marissa —

We observed a sudden production degradation on our private VPC cluster starting ~04:00 UTC this morning. Symptoms: p99 latency jumped from ~420ms to ~1.8s, 502/5xx rate increased to ~4.5% (baseline <0.5%), and aggregate throughput has dropped ~30% across inference endpoints.

Our SREs have attached a small sample log and a dashboard screenshot for reference (error-sample.log, metrics-screenshot.png). Traffic profile: no major traffic spike from our end; appears to be many long-context chat sessions.

This is impacting our customers — we need urgent help. Can Redwood join an on-call bridge? Also please confirm if there was any config change or rollout on your side last night.

Thanks,
Priya
Soliq Health — Head of Platform

Subject: Triage notes - Soliq Health private cluster (initial)

Team — quick triage summary from the bridge and initial log dives:

Findings:
- Error class: majority are 502s surfaced at the runtime layer, tied to KV cache misses during context assembly; traces show repeated cache miss -> fetch -> eviction loops.
- Workload: high proportion of long-context sessions (avg seq len ~ 6k tokens for a subset), causing increased KV footprint per request.
- No recent infra kernel rollouts flagged in our deployment logs; config diffs are clear since last night.

Hypothesis: sudden change in request mix is causing K/V cache pressure and high eviction churn; this in turn increases CPU on the worker and pushes some requests to error paths under tail latency.

Immediate mitigations proposed (can be done remotely, low-risk):
1) Reduce per-shard concurrency from 48 -> 28 for the affected deployment (expected to reduce thrash).
2) Increase KV cache high-water mark by 20% and enable explicit prefix caching for the top 30 prefixes.
3) Canary route 25% traffic to the quantized model variant (lower mem footprint) — measure 5xx/p99 delta.
4) If the above doesn't show improvement within 45m, schedule rolling restarts of worker pods (2-hour window; requires customer approval due to KMS/HSM integration for secrets).

Requested from Soliq: sign-off for the rolling restart window if needed and permission to perform the 25% canary routing change now.

Attaching triage-notes-olga.txt (short logs + kernel traces).

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Exec sync: Soliq Health private cluster — remediation & credit proposal

Folks — brief exec summary and ask. Soliq Health (RDW-4987) is in production-impacting state after the KV-cache eviction pattern triggered p99 latencies and 5xx spikes on their private VPC cluster. Timeline: incident first observed 2026-10-18 11:00 UTC; triage showed cache evictions associated with a change in request mix (long-context sessions).

What we've done:
- Enabled 25% canary routing to quantized variant (observed immediate ~60% reduction in 5xx for canary traffic).
- Applied per-shard concurrency reduction and increased KV cache high-water mark — p95 improved but p99 still above SLA.
- Gathered logs and traces; triage notes attached.

Ask for exec approval:
1) Authorize a 2-hour rolling restart of worker nodes tonight (required due to KMS rekey handshake and impacts on session affinity). Customer has given conditional sign-off but needs exec-level assurance on timing.
2) Approve a customer credit as a goodwill make-good: proposed 20% credit of the October invoice for production hours impacted (we estimate 6-10 hours).
3) Approve an accelerated post-mortem and a short-term engineering ticket priority: improve KV cache eviction heuristic and add aggressive prefix warming for long-context workloads.

Attached: exec-brief-solihq.pdf (one-page summary, impact numbers, canary graphs).

Recommendation: grant restart approval tonight (we plan rolling restarts in 10m windows per rack to reduce blast radius) and approve the 20% credit. We will publish a 72-hour incident report and a remediation timeline.

Please reply with APPROVE / DENY and any alternate credit guidance.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Site Reliability, Redwood Inference
